name: Travel Risk API
description:
Real-time travel advisories, disaster alerts, conflict events and composite country risk scores, aggregated from government and multilateral sources.

## Authentication
Send your key in the `X-API-Key` header on every `/api/v1/*` request:

```
curl -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" \
  https://api.travelriskapi.com/api/v1/alerts?limit=5
```

No key yet? `POST /api/v1/register` with `{"email": "you@example.com"}` returns one immediately and emails you a copy. Lost it? `POST /api/v1/recover-key`.

## Plans and limits
| Plan | Price | Requests/day | Burst/min |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 100 | 60 |
| Starter | $29/mo | 2,000 | 120 |
| Pro | $99/mo | 10,000 | 600 |
| Enterprise | $499/mo | unlimited | 3,000 |

The same key also opens the aviation API (`/api/v9`, `/adb`, `/ext/v1`): flight status, airports, airlines, airline safety, in-flight Wi-Fi and Starlink, airport security wait times. Reference: https://api.travelriskapi.com/ext/reference/

Credits (from $10 for 10,000 requests, no subscription) are consumed only after the daily quota is exhausted, so they act as overflow. See `GET /api/v1/billing/plans`.

The daily counter resets at 00:00 UTC. Two independent limits apply — a per-minute burst limit and the daily quota — and each returns `429` with `Retry-After`.

## Response headers
| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-Quota-Limit` / `X-Quota-Used` / `X-Quota-Remaining` | your daily allowance |
| `X-Credits-Balance` | prepaid credits left |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | per-minute burst |
| `X-Cache` | `HIT` or `MISS` — responses are cached server-side for 15 minutes |
| `ETag`, `Age` | cache metadata (informational) |

`Cache-Control: no-cache` is intentional: we cache on our side to answer faster, but you always reach us, so you never receive data your own HTTP library held back.

## Risk scores
An `advisory_level` of **0** means no source publishes an advisory for that territory (small dependencies, some overseas territories) — treat it as no data, not as risk-free. Published levels are 1-4.

`risk_score` is a composite on a 1-5 scale: the advisory level plus up to +2.0 from currently active alerts, with diminishing returns: impact = 2 * (1 - exp(-w / 4)), where w weighs each alert by severity (Critical 1.0, High 0.5, Medium 0.25, Low 0) and local zone-level warnings (US National Weather Service counties) at 1/20. Capped at 5.0. The same value is returned by `/countries` and `/risk-score/{iso}` — they share one implementation. `/countries` also exposes `base_risk_score` (the advisory level alone) and `active_alerts` so you can see how a score was reached.

## Tracking changes
List responses also carry `data_updated_at` (the newest record we hold) and `generated_at` (when this payload was assembled), so freshness is explicit. Conflict data is pulled every 15 minutes, alerts every 6 hours, government advisories daily.

Alert ids are stable: when an upstream revises an alert (severity escalates, wording changes), we update the same record and bump `updated_at` rather than issuing a new id. To sync incrementally, poll with `updated_since`:

```
GET /api/v1/alerts?updated_since=2026-08-26T00:00:00&limit=1000
```

That returns alerts created **or** revised since that moment. Keep the highest `updated_at` you have seen and pass it back next time. `created_at` never moves, so `updated_at > created_at` means the alert has been revised at least once.

## Country codes
Endpoints taking a country accept **ISO 3166-1 alpha-3** (`USA`, `GBR`, `FRA`). For convenience **alpha-2** (`US`, `GB`) is also accepted, as are the legacy 3-letter codes this API used before 2026-08-11. `GET /api/v1/countries/codes` returns every supported code in one response.

## Changelog
Every API change is listed at https://travelriskapi.com/changelog — including new fields, which are the most likely thing to surprise a strict JSON parser. We add fields; we do not rename or remove them without notice, and **API keys do not expire**.

## Pagination
List endpoints take `skip` and `limit` (max **1000** per page) and report `total`, so a full export of ~19,000 alerts takes 20 requests and a few seconds. Responses are compressed (gzip/zstd) when your client advertises support.
